apex_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A folder of Apex Legends text log files, if it exists at this path.
apex_cache.used_for: Logs are only read for troubleshooting; the game writes new ones on its next run.
apex_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
apex_cache.catalog_concern: The label promises a 'shader preload', but the only path is a logs folder. Apex keeps its settings and profile under Saved Games\Respawn\Apex (local, profile) -- that folder must never be targeted.

arma_cache.what: %APPDATA%\Arma 3 / %LOCALAPPDATA%\Arma 3 are Arma 3's whole data folders: .RPT logs plus profile settings, mission cache and other per-user data.
arma_cache.used_for: The game reads profile data and settings from here on every launch.
arma_cache.risk: Deleting the whole folder loses profile settings and local data, not just logs.
arma_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the paths are whole app data folders. Only the *.rpt log files would be a safe target.

battle_net_auth_cache.what: Cache, web cache and log folders under %APPDATA%\Blizzard\Battle.net. Current Battle.net does not use these paths: its caches are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Battle.net and %ProgramData%\Battle.net (checked on this PC).
battle_net_auth_cache.used_for: Blizzard says removing the Battle.net cache does not touch game data; the app rebuilds it on its next start.
battle_net_auth_cache.risk: If the paths exist: a slower first start of the app and lost logs. No sign-out.
battle_net_auth_cache.before_cleaning: Close Battle.net and end Agent.exe first.
battle_net_auth_cache.catalog_concern: The label says 'authentication ticket cache': that would sign you out, but nothing here is one. The paths are stale and find nothing on a current install; battlenet_local_caches is the entry that matches real folders. Never add %LOCALAPPDATA%\Battle.net\Account (it holds cookie.bin, the sign-in).

battlenet_cache.what: Cache, web cache and log folders under %APPDATA%\Blizzard\Battle.net. Current Battle.net does not use these paths: its caches are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Battle.net and %ProgramData%\Battle.net (checked on this PC).
battlenet_cache.used_for: Blizzard says removing the Battle.net cache does not touch game data; the app rebuilds it on its next start.
battlenet_cache.risk: If the paths exist: a slower first start of the app and lost logs. No sign-out.
battlenet_cache.before_cleaning: Close Battle.net and end Agent.exe first.
battlenet_cache.catalog_concern: The paths are stale and find nothing on a current install; battlenet_local_caches is the entry that matches real folders. Never add %LOCALAPPDATA%\Battle.net\Account (it holds cookie.bin, the sign-in).

battlenet_local_caches.what: Battle.net's Cache folder and the Cache/Code Cache/DawnCache/GPUCache of each embedded-browser profile under BrowserCaches (verified on this PC).
battlenet_local_caches.used_for: Rebuilt on the app's next start; Blizzard says clearing the cache does not affect game data.
battlenet_local_caches.risk: Slower first start. No sign-out: Local Storage, Network and Session Storage beside them, and Account\cookie.bin, are not touched.

beamng_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. BeamNG.drive log files, if they exist at this path.
beamng_cache.used_for: Diagnostics only; new logs are written on the next launch.
beamng_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
beamng_cache.catalog_concern: BeamNG's user folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\BeamNG.drive\<version>) holds mods, vehicle configs and saves; keeping it out is correct.

blizzard_downloads_cache.what: Battle.net and Diablo III log folders (paths that a current install mostly does not use).
blizzard_downloads_cache.used_for: Logs are only for troubleshooting and are recreated.
blizzard_downloads_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
blizzard_downloads_cache.before_cleaning: Close Battle.net and the game first.
blizzard_downloads_cache.catalog_concern: The label promises 'patch staging and manifest cache', but only log folders are listed. Real patch data lives inside the game folders and must not be deleted (it would force a re-download or repair).

bsd_wine_cache.what: A duplicate of the Battle.net cache/webcache/log paths.
bsd_wine_cache.used_for: Same as battlenet_cache: rebuildable cache and logs.
bsd_wine_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling is harmless (it duplicates battlenet_cache), but the stated reason (whole data folder or sign-in store) does not describe these paths.

cities_skylines_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Cities: Skylines log files, if present at this path (the game normally writes output_log.txt inside its install folder).
cities_skylines_cache.used_for: Diagnostics only; rewritten on next start.
cities_skylines_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
cities_skylines_cache.catalog_concern: Correctly excludes %LOCALAPPDATA%\Colossal Order\Cities_Skylines, which holds saves, maps and mods.

ck2_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Crusader Kings II log files. Paradox games normally write logs to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings II\logs, so this %APPDATA% path may not exist.
ck2_cache.used_for: Logs (error.log, game.log ...) are rewritten every launch and only help troubleshooting.
ck2_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
ck2_cache.before_cleaning: Close the game and the Paradox Launcher first.
ck2_cache.catalog_concern: The label mentions 'replay cache and DLC download staging'; the path is only logs. Never widen this to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings II: save games and mods live there.

ck3_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Crusader Kings III log files. Paradox games normally write logs to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\logs, so this %APPDATA% path may not exist.
ck3_cache.used_for: Logs (error.log, game.log ...) are rewritten every launch and only help troubleshooting.
ck3_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
ck3_cache.before_cleaning: Close the game and the Paradox Launcher first.
ck3_cache.catalog_concern: Never widen this to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III: save games and mods live there.

csgo_cache.what: ...\csgo\local\cfg holds Counter-Strike's CONFIG files (keybinds, settings, autoexec), not a cache. The path under %APPDATA% does not exist on normal installs.
csgo_cache.used_for: The game reads these configs on every launch.
csgo_cache.risk: Lost keybinds, video and game settings.
csgo_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: cfg is user configuration. CS2's shader cache is in Steam's shadercache\730 instead.

curseforge_cache.what: CurseForge's Chromium/Electron caches: Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache, Dawn GPU caches and blob_storage (verified present on this PC next to IndexedDB, Local Storage and Network, which are NOT listed).

destiny2_cache.what: Bungie's Destiny 2 user folders: settings (cvars.xml) and the activity feed data.
destiny2_cache.used_for: Read on every launch; deleting resets settings.
destiny2_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: these are whole app data folders.

diablo4_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Diablo IV log folders, if present (Diablo IV keeps settings in Documents\Diablo IV).
diablo4_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
diablo4_cache.before_cleaning: Close Diablo IV and Battle.net first.
diablo4_cache.catalog_concern: The label promises a 'shader cache', but the paths are logs only. That is the safer choice: the real shader cache rebuild causes stutter.

ea_app_cache.what: Cache and log folders of the EA app and the older Origin client (web cache, launcher logs). Several listed paths are older layouts; current EA app caches are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop and %ProgramData%\EA Desktop.
ea_app_cache.used_for: EA's own 'App Recovery > Clear Cache' clears the same kind of data; the app rebuilds it on its next start.
ea_app_cache.risk: A slower first start and lost logs. Game installs are not here.
ea_app_cache.before_cleaning: Quit the EA app (also from the tray) first.
ea_app_cache.catalog_concern: Some paths are stale. Only Cache/logs/WebCache are listed, which is correct; never add the EA Desktop root folders.

ea_desktop_full_cache.what: EA app Cache and logs folders (older paths).
ea_desktop_full_cache.used_for: Same as ea_app_cache: rebuilt on next start.
ea_desktop_full_cache.risk: A slower first start and lost logs.
ea_desktop_full_cache.catalog_concern: The label says 'game content staging' -- download staging would cost a re-download, but the paths do not include any.

epic_games_cache.what: Epic Games Launcher web cache, a data cache and its logs.
epic_games_cache.used_for: Epic tells users to delete the Saved\webcache folders to fix display or launcher errors; they are rebuilt on next start.
epic_games_cache.risk: A slower first launcher start; lost logs. No sign-out, games untouched.
epic_games_cache.before_cleaning: Exit the Epic Games Launcher from the tray first.
epic_games_cache.catalog_concern: The label says 'shader compiler staging and manifest data' -- wrong. Data\Manifests (the list of installed games) must never be targeted, or the launcher forgets installed games.

epic_launcher_cache.what: Same Epic Launcher webcache, data cache and logs as epic_games_cache.
epic_launcher_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is fine, but the reason given (user data / sign-in store) is wrong for these paths: webcache is exactly what Epic says to delete.

epic_manifest_cache.what: The Epic Games Launcher log folder only.
epic_manifest_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
epic_manifest_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'manifest data and download URL cache' but only logs are listed -- good, since deleting real manifests makes the launcher forget installed games.

eso_cache.what: Elder Scrolls Online log files. The listed path (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Documents\...) is malformed; ESO uses Documents\Elder Scrolls Online\live\Logs.
eso_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
eso_cache.catalog_concern: The path will not match. If fixed, target only live\Logs: live\AddOns and live\SavedVariables hold add-ons and their saved data.

eu4_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Europa Universalis IV log files. Paradox games normally write logs to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Europa Universalis IV\logs, so this %APPDATA% path may not exist.
eu4_cache.used_for: Logs (error.log, game.log ...) are rewritten every launch and only help troubleshooting.
eu4_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
eu4_cache.before_cleaning: Close the game and the Paradox Launcher first.
eu4_cache.catalog_concern: Never widen this to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Europa Universalis IV: save games and mods live there.

fortnite_cache.what: A D3D shader cache under FortniteGame\Saved, plus %LOCALAPPDATA%\Frostbite\Cache (Frostbite is EA's engine, not Fortnite's).
fortnite_cache.used_for: Compiled GPU shaders; deleting them forces recompilation. Epic warns the first match after clearing a shader cache may stutter.
fortnite_cache.risk: Stutter and longer loads until shaders recompile; nothing is lost permanently.
fortnite_cache.before_cleaning: Close Fortnite and the Epic launcher. Only worth doing when stutter is suspected to come from a bad cache.
fortnite_cache.catalog_concern: Shader caches should be 'caution', not 'safe': clearing costs stutter. The Frostbite path belongs to EA games, not Fortnite.

forza_cache.what: Forza Horizon / Motorsport data folders: settings, saves, clips and the photo/capture gallery.
forza_cache.risk: Lost saves, settings, clips and photos.
forza_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: these are whole user-data folders.

game_bar_widget_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A Game Bar data folder.
game_bar_widget_cache.risk: Unknown -- could reset Game Bar settings.
game_bar_widget_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a whole app folder, not a named cache.

gamejolt_cache.what: Game Jolt client's whole data folder, including installed games and sign-in data.
gamejolt_cache.used_for: Used by the client on every start.
gamejolt_cache.risk: Sign-out and possibly deleted installed games.
gamejolt_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a whole app folder.

gamepass_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A Game Bar logs folder (this path is not used by current Xbox/Game Bar builds).
gamepass_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
gamepass_cache.catalog_concern: Label promises 'downloads and shader cache' but the path is a logs folder; Game Pass game installs (XboxGames) must never be targeted.

gog_cache.what: GOG Galaxy Cache, WebCache and logs folders. Current Galaxy keeps these under %ProgramData%\GOG.com\Galaxy (webcache, logs), so the %APPDATA% paths may not exist.
gog_cache.used_for: GOG forum advice for a stuck client is to clear webcache first; it is rebuilt. Logs are diagnostics.
gog_cache.before_cleaning: Exit GOG Galaxy (also from the tray) first.
gog_cache.catalog_concern: Never widen to %ProgramData%\GOG.com\Galaxy\storage: galaxy-2.0.db there is the library database (playtime, tags, connected platforms).

gog_galaxy2_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is fine; the stated reason (user data) does not describe these paths.

gog_offline_cache.what: GOG Galaxy Cache and logs folders (same as gog_cache).
gog_offline_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'offline installer cache and game backup metadata' -- downloaded offline installers/backups are user data, but no such path is listed.

hoi4_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Hearts of Iron IV log files. Paradox games normally write logs to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Hearts of Iron IV\logs, so this %APPDATA% path may not exist.
hoi4_cache.used_for: Logs (error.log, game.log ...) are rewritten every launch and only help troubleshooting.
hoi4_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
hoi4_cache.before_cleaning: Close the game and the Paradox Launcher first.
hoi4_cache.catalog_concern: The label mentions a 'replay cache'; the path is only logs. Never widen this to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Hearts of Iron IV: save games and mods live there.

humble_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Cache and logs of the Humble App (an Electron app).
humble_cache.used_for: Chromium-style Cache is rebuilt on next start; logs are diagnostics.
humble_cache.catalog_concern: Fine as long as only Cache/logs are listed; Local Storage/IndexedDB beside them would sign you out.

humble_choice_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is fine; the reason text does not match the paths.

itch_app_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The itch.io app's logs folder.
itch_app_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
itch_app_cache.catalog_concern: Label promises 'cache, downloads, community data' but only logs are listed -- good; itch's installed games and sign-in must not be touched.

itch_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
itch_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is fine.

kongregate_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a whole app folder.

lol_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. League of Legends logs, if present at this %APPDATA% path (LoL normally logs inside its install folder).
lol_cache.used_for: Diagnostics; Riot support asks for these when troubleshooting.
lol_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
lol_cache.before_cleaning: Close League and the Riot Client first.
lol_cache.catalog_concern: The label mentions a 'replay cache': replays (.rofl in Documents\League of Legends\Replays) are user data and must never be targeted; none are listed.

lutris_cache.what: Lutris (a Linux game manager) Wine prefixes and runners. Not used on Windows.
lutris_cache.used_for: A Wine prefix holds installed games and their saves.
lutris_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: Wine prefixes are installs plus saves, and Lutris does not run on Windows.

lutris_runs_cache.what: Lutris runners, Wine prefixes and its share folder (Linux only).
lutris_runs_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: same as lutris_cache.

minecraft_cache.what: Minecraft Java's logs folder (latest.log and gzipped older logs).
minecraft_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
minecraft_cache.catalog_concern: Label promises 'shader cache, resource pack staging'; only logs are listed -- good. .minecraft\saves, screenshots, resourcepacks and shaderpacks are user data.

minecraft_launcher_cache.what: Minecraft Java logs and crash-reports folders.
minecraft_launcher_cache.used_for: Crash reports explain past crashes; both are recreated as needed.

minedrive_cache.what: Minesweeper data and the Phone Link (YourPhone) app folder.
minedrive_cache.used_for: Phone Link stores its phone pairing and synced data.
minedrive_cache.risk: Phone Link unpairs / loses synced data.
minedrive_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: YourPhone is Phone Link's data, not a game cache.

oculus_cache.what: Meta/Oculus whole data folder (and a bogus registry-like path).
oculus_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a whole app folder.

overwatch_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Overwatch logs and a Cache folder under %APPDATA%\Blizzard\Overwatch, if present.
overwatch_cache.risk: Lost logs; a slower first start.
overwatch_cache.catalog_concern: Overwatch keeps its settings in Documents\Overwatch\Settings -- never target that.

paradox_cache.what: Paradox launcher apps folder and the user's mods folder.
paradox_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: it pointed at mods.

path_of_exile_cache.what: Path of Exile logs and its compiled shader cache (shaderCache).
path_of_exile_cache.used_for: Shaders are recompiled after deletion; community and GGG forum guides clear it only to fix a corrupt cache.
path_of_exile_cache.risk: Stutter and FPS drops until the shader cache is rebuilt; logs lost. Nothing permanent.
path_of_exile_cache.before_cleaning: Close the game. Only when the cache is suspected corrupt.
path_of_exile_cache.catalog_concern: Shader cache should be 'caution', not 'safe' (rebuild stutter). PoE 1 actually uses %APPDATA%\Path of Exile (and PoE 2 %APPDATA%\Path of Exile 2\ShaderCache*), so the Grinding Gear Games path may not match.

protonvpn_cache.what: Proton VPN's whole data folder (settings, account/session data and logs), misfiled under games.
protonvpn_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a whole app folder holding sign-in data; only a logs subfolder could ever be a target.

pubg_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. PUBG (TslGame) logs and crash-reporter files.
pubg_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup. Crash reports not yet sent are lost.

rimworld_cache.what: RimWorld's user folder: Saves, Config (settings, mod list) and the player log.
rimworld_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: it holds saves.

roblox_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Roblox log files and an installer download folder.
roblox_cache.used_for: Logs are diagnostics; downloads are re-fetched by the bootstrapper if needed.
roblox_cache.risk: Lost logs; a possible re-download on update.

rockstar_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Rockstar Games Launcher logs.
rockstar_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
rockstar_cache.catalog_concern: Label promises Social Club cache and updates; only logs are listed. Documents\Rockstar Games holds saves and settings -- never target.

rust_game_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Rust logs and crash-reports, if present at this path.
rust_game_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
rust_game_cache.catalog_concern: Label mentions 'shader cache' but none is listed.

steamCMD_cache.what: SteamCMD folders: downloaded dedicated-server/game content and workshop items.
steamCMD_cache.risk: Lost server installs (re-download of many GB).
steamCMD_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: downloaded content, not cache.

steam_cache.what: Steam's per-game shader pre-cache (shadercache) and the Steam client's embedded-browser data folder (htmlcache), under a non-default Steam location.
steam_cache.used_for: Shaders are re-downloaded/recompiled per game; htmlcache is the Steam store/community browser profile.
steam_cache.risk: Stutter until shaders rebuild. The WHOLE htmlcache also holds Cookies, Local Storage and Login Data of the Steam web views.
steam_cache.catalog_concern: Shader cache should be 'caution'. Whole htmlcache is a Chromium profile with cookies (on this PC %LOCALAPPDATA%\Steam\htmlcache\Default holds Cookies/Login Data/Local Storage); target only its Cache/Code Cache/GPUCache, as steam_webhelper_caches does. %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Steam is not Steam's default location.

steam_cloud_sync_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A non-existent steamapps\backups path.
steam_cloud_sync_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a 'backups' folder is user data by name.

steam_deck_cache.what: Game installs (steamapps\common) and a steamdeck folder.
steam_deck_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: steamapps\common is games.

steam_download_cache.what: Steam's in-progress download staging and the whole htmlcache browser profile.
steam_download_cache.used_for: Partial downloads resume from scratch; htmlcache holds web-view sign-in data.
steam_download_cache.risk: Re-download of interrupted updates; sign-in data in htmlcache (Cookies/Local Storage).
steam_download_cache.before_cleaning: Exit Steam and make sure nothing is downloading.
steam_download_cache.catalog_concern: Same htmlcache problem as steam_cache; the downloads path is non-default (Steam stages in steamapps\downloading).

steam_full_cache.what: Steam logs, shader pre-cache, download staging and the whole htmlcache folder.
steam_full_cache.used_for: Mix of diagnostics, rebuildable shaders and a browser profile.
steam_full_cache.risk: Shader stutter, re-downloads of interrupted updates, possible loss of Steam web-view cookies.
steam_full_cache.before_cleaning: Exit Steam; no download in progress.
steam_full_cache.catalog_concern: Bundles shader cache and whole htmlcache under 'safe'. Split it: logs safe, shaders caution, htmlcache only its Cache subfolders.

steam_logs.what: Steam client log files in the Steam install folder (connection, content, bootstrap logs).
steam_logs.used_for: Diagnostics; Valve support may ask for them. Steam writes new ones.
steam_logs.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
steam_logs.before_cleaning: Exit Steam first (files are held open).

steam_proton_cache.what: Proton compatdata: one Wine prefix per game, containing that game's saves and settings.
steam_proton_cache.risk: Lost saves and settings for non-Steam-Cloud games.
steam_proton_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: compatdata holds saves.

steam_shader_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling is right; as written it would also take the whole htmlcache.

steam_webhelper_cache.what: The Steam web-helper's whole htmlcache folder (a Chromium profile). The real one is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Steam\htmlcache; %APPDATA%\Steam does not exist on this PC.
steam_webhelper_cache.used_for: Steam's store, library and community pages run in this embedded browser.
steam_webhelper_cache.risk: The profile holds Cookies, Local Storage, Session Storage and Login Data: deleting it all signs out the Steam web views.
steam_webhelper_cache.catalog_concern: Targets the whole Chromium profile, not just caches; steam_webhelper_caches is the correct, narrow version.

steam_webhelper_caches.what: Only the cache subfolders of Steam's embedded browser: Default\Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache and the Chromium shader caches (verified on this PC).
steam_webhelper_caches.used_for: Rebuilt when Steam's store/library pages are opened again; these GPU shader caches are for Steam's UI, not games.
steam_webhelper_caches.risk: Slightly slower Steam UI first time. No sign-out: Cookies, Login Data and Local Storage are not touched.

steamvr_cache.what: SteamVR folder and Steam's config folder (config.vdf, loginusers.vdf).
steamvr_cache.used_for: Steam's config holds sign-in and client settings.
steamvr_cache.risk: Steam signs out and loses settings; SteamVR loses room setup.
steamvr_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: Steam\config is Steam's sign-in and settings store.

stellaris_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Stellaris log files. Paradox games normally write logs to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Stellaris\logs, so this %APPDATA% path may not exist.
stellaris_cache.used_for: Logs (error.log, game.log ...) are rewritten every launch and only help troubleshooting.
stellaris_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
stellaris_cache.before_cleaning: Close the game and the Paradox Launcher first.
stellaris_cache.catalog_concern: The label says 'game save staging' -- wrong and alarming; the path is only logs. Never widen this to Documents\Paradox Interactive\Stellaris: save games and mods live there.

terraria_cache.what: %APPDATA%\Re-Logic: Re-Logic's whole user-data folder (Terraria/tModLoader data, settings and backups; players and worlds are normally in Documents\My Games\Terraria).
terraria_cache.risk: Possible loss of characters/worlds or settings.
terraria_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: a whole user-data folder.

ubisoft_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Ubisoft Connect cache, downloads, logs and shader-cache folders under %APPDATA%/%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ubisoft\Connect (current installs keep their cache in the launcher folder in Program Files (x86)).
ubisoft_cache.used_for: The launcher re-creates caches; a 'downloads' folder would be game download staging.
ubisoft_cache.risk: Possible re-download of a paused game download; shader-cache rebuild stutter; users report having to sign in again after clearing the launcher cache.
ubisoft_cache.before_cleaning: Quit Ubisoft Connect; no download in progress.
ubisoft_cache.catalog_concern: 'downloads' and 'shader-cache' are not 'safe' items. Paths look unverified.

unity_cache.what: Unity Editor/Hub cache and log folders under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Unity.
unity_cache.used_for: Unity documents its caches (package and build caches) as rebuildable; logs (Editor.log) are diagnostics.
unity_cache.risk: Packages re-download and builds/imports take longer next time; lost logs.
unity_cache.before_cleaning: Close the Unity Editor and Hub first.
unity_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'library' -- a project's Library folder is not here and should not be. %APPDATA%\Unity\Asset Store-5.x (downloaded assets) is not listed, correctly.

unity_hub_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Unity Hub cache and logs (Hub actually lives in %APPDATA%\UnityHub, an Electron profile).
unity_hub_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'downloaded editor installs' -- those are installs, not cache; none are listed. Never widen to the Hub profile root (Local Storage = sign-in).

unity_hub_full_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling as a duplicate is fine.

unreal_cache.what: Unreal Engine's local Derived Data Cache (compiled shaders, cooked textures and other derived data).
unreal_cache.used_for: Epic: DDC content is disposable and is regenerated from the .uasset files.
unreal_cache.risk: Opening projects is much slower afterwards (shader compilation can take a long time). Nothing is lost.
unreal_cache.catalog_concern: The label mentions 'build, intermediate, and saved folders' -- a project's Saved holds autosaves and config; it is not targeted, correctly.

valorant_cache.what: Intended: VALORANT and Vanguard logs. Riot documents the logs at %LOCALAPPDATA%\VALORANT\Saved\Logs.
valorant_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
valorant_cache.catalog_concern: Both paths are wrong ('Riot Games\Valorant\logs' under %APPDATA%, and a typo 'Signip'), so the entry finds nothing.

warcraft_cache.what: World of Warcraft, Diablo III and Hearthstone log folders (WoW actually writes Logs inside its install folder, e.g. _retail_\Logs).
warcraft_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.
warcraft_cache.before_cleaning: Close the games and Battle.net first.
warcraft_cache.catalog_concern: WoW's WTF folder (add-on settings, keybinds, macros) and Interface\AddOns must never be targeted; they are not.

warframe_cache.what: Warframe's whole data folders (EE.log plus EE.cfg settings and other data).
warframe_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: whole app folders; only EE.log would be safe.

windows_game_bar_cache.what: XboxLive folder and Xbox Game Overlay LocalCache.
windows_game_bar_cache.used_for: Xbox sign-in tokens/device data may live here.
windows_game_bar_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: may hold sign-in data.

winehq_cache.what: Wine (Linux) temp folder and cache. These paths do not exist on Windows.

wineprefix_cache.what: Whole Wine/PlayOnLinux prefixes and winetricks downloads (Linux).
wineprefix_cache.used_for: Prefixes hold installed programs and saves.

xbox_app_cache.what: Gaming Services and Xbox Game Bar package LocalCache folders.
xbox_app_cache.risk: Could break game launching or sign-in until repaired.
xbox_app_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: Gaming Services state is not a plain cache.

xbox_cache.what: Gaming Services and Game Bar LocalCache, Family notifications LocalState and %ProgramData%\XboxLiveDeviceInfo.
xbox_cache.risk: Xbox sign-in / device identity reset; family settings state lost.
xbox_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: LocalState and device info are not caches.

xbox_live_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A Game Bar logs folder at a path current Windows does not use.
xbox_live_cache.risk: Only past diagnostics are lost: support or a crash investigation can no longer read what happened before the cleanup.

steam_appcache_httpcache.what: Steam client HTTP cache inside appcache, observed on this PC. Valve's tracker lists appcache/httpcache as a cache on Linux; Valve does not document the Windows path.
steam_appcache_httpcache.used_for: Showing store and library artwork and pages without downloading them again.
steam_appcache_httpcache.risk: Library and store images load more slowly once while Steam downloads them again. Games, saves, sign-in and appinfo.vdf are not in this folder.
steam_appcache_httpcache.before_cleaning: Close Steam for a complete clean; files it holds open are skipped.
steam_appcache_httpcache.catalog_concern: Valve documents depots but not these Windows cache paths. Directory evidence is a user report in Valve's tracker, corroborated by this PC. Only common fixed-drive Steam install roots are covered; arbitrary custom install folders are not.

steam_depotcache.what: Steam depot manifest cache observed on this PC. Valve documents depots as game-content groups; the depotcache directory is also listed in Valve's Linux tracker, but its Windows path is not officially documented.
steam_depotcache.used_for: Starting and checking game downloads and updates. Steam fetches a manifest again when it needs one.
steam_depotcache.risk: A paused or running download or update may have to start over or verify again. Installed games and saves are not stored here.
steam_depotcache.before_cleaning: Close Steam and make sure no download or update is queued. Manifests younger than a day are kept.
steam_depotcache.catalog_concern: Valve documents depots, not this Windows path. Directory evidence is a user report in Valve's tracker, corroborated by this PC. Only the default install root is approved by the catalog audit allowlist; custom roots require a separate allowlist review.
